newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises on longer-term loans.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises on longer-term loans.

text.p: The average lending rate rose 50 points to 9.4 percent on Friday, boosted by longer-term bank borrowings at higher rates on Croatia's money market.
Three-month funds were placed at 15 percent and one-month at 12 percent. Call money rates ranged between 8.0 and 10 percent. Insurers' short-term rate was flat at 7.0 percent.
Total settlements shrank to 26 million kuna but most were new loans, dealers said. Supply was also lower at 80 million kuna.
Overnight trade totalled 127.4 million kuna on Thursday as three banks borrowed money to cover their shortfalls.

The National Bank of Croatia stayed out of the foreign exchange market. The kuna midrate eased to 5.3867 from 5.3720 to the dollar while firming marginally to 3.5537 against the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
